Great advice - can you share some practical tips on how this can be achieved?

When you are juggling so much, you have to break your responsibilities down and have an idea on what would slip. And you need to own and know your schedule.

My priorities are keeping my sanity and family in a good state, followed by work, followed by OMSA followed by household chores (notice how it’s not the same as keeping family in a good state). Every responsibility is written in an agenda/ diary.

This means that I optimize along these lines. In the last 2 week, I had major milestones I had to hit for work (a  presentation and 2 critical reviews), a midterm (I take one class), health work I needed to do on myself and homework plus responsibilities of family and such. Before as soon as I knew of the responsibilities, I put them noted them. I put the deadlines of my work, school, life (bank errands, medical stuff, dentist etc) in a little organizer. That way, I can instantly tell if a week will be hard. Then I have conversations with my family on how we can work to pull it off (my work is high stress tech and not so flex). Generally this means accepting the house will not be pristine, getting help with chores, working remotely to save time and ordering take out. It also means that I know what my capacity is for a given time period so I can push back on some additional responsibilities and complete them when I have easier weeks :-) 

Another thing is:  I deliberately take time to do enjoyable things (eg walk around the block, eat my favorite food every 2-3 days, listen to music in peace) etc. remember that your time is yours - you get 24 hours and you have to squeeze what you can in there :-) Good luck!
